title: Demo Call 1: Diarrhea after a missed dose (Dupixent, asthma)

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: Hi, this is Alex, a pharmacist with the patient management program at Demo Specialty Pharmacy. Is this Jordan?

lines.speaker: patient
lines.text: Hi, yes, this is Jordan.

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: Great, and just so you know, this call is being recorded.

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: Before we continue, can you confirm your date of birth for privacy?

lines.speaker: patient
lines.text: Sure, it's January 1st, 2002.

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: Thank you for confirming that. You're currently taking Dupixent, one 300 mg injection under the skin every 2 weeks. We like to check in and see how you're doing and whether you've had any side effects or any other issues. If you report any side effects or product complaints, we report them to the manufacturer. If they have follow-up questions, would it be alright if they contacted you or your doctor?

lines.speaker: patient
lines.text: They can contact my doctor, not me.

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: No problem, I'll note that. Have you had any side effects or missed any doses?

lines.speaker: patient
lines.text: Yes, I missed last night's dose. I usually take my shot on Friday every other week, but last night I got out of work late. I've also had some diarrhea.

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Working late is understandable. How long has the diarrhea been going on?

lines.speaker: patient
lines.text: About a day, just today and yesterday.

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: Have you tried anything?

lines.speaker: patient
lines.text: Not really.

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: I understand. Just remember with diarrhea to keep replacing fluids and electrolytes. Bland foods like bananas and applesauce can help, and you can use Imodium if needed. If it lasts more than two days, or you get a fever of 102 or higher or signs of dehydration, contact your doctor. Since you missed last night's dose, you can inject it now because it's within 7 days, and then keep your regular schedule.

lines.speaker: patient
lines.text: Okay, that makes sense.

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: Have you been to the ER or hospital recently?

lines.speaker: patient
lines.text: Nope.

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: Good to hear. Remember to tell your doctor about any side effects, and call 911 if you ever have a serious emergency. Is there anything else I can help with?

lines.speaker: patient
lines.text: No, that's all. Thank you.

lines.speaker: pharmacist
lines.text: Thank you so much for speaking with me today. We'll check back in a couple of months, but you can always reach out if needed. Have a good day.
